In [[algebraic number theory]], '''Leopoldt's conjecture''', introduced by [[Heinrich-Wolfgang Leopoldt]],{{sfnp|Leopoldt|1962}}{{sfnp|Leopoldt|1975}} states that the [[p-adic numbers|''p''-adic]] regulator of a [[Algebraic number field|number field]] does not vanish. The ''p''-adic regulator is an analogue of the usual 
[[Regulator_(mathematics)|regulator]] defined using [[p-adic exponential function#p-adic logarithm function|''p''-adic logarithms]] instead of the usual logarithms.

==Formulation==

Let ''K'' be a [[number field]] and for each [[prime number|prime]] ''P'' of ''K'' above some fixed rational prime ''p'', let ''U''<sub>''P''</sub> denote the local [[unit (ring theory)|units]] at ''P'' and let ''U''<sub>1,''P''</sub> denote the subgroup of principal units in ''U''<sub>''P''</sub>. Set

:<math>U_1 = \prod_{P\,\mid\, p} U_{1,P}.</math>

Then let ''E''<sub>1</sub> denote the set of global units ''ε'' that map to ''U''<sub>1</sub> via the [[diagonal embedding]] of the global units in&nbsp;''E''.

Since ''E''<sub>1</sub> is a finite-[[Index of a subgroup|index]] subgroup of the global units, it is an [[abelian group]] of rank ''r''<sub>1</sub> + ''r''<sub>2</sub> – 1, where ''r''<sub>1</sub> is the number of real embeddings of ''K'' and ''r''<sub>2</sub> the number of pairs of complex embeddings. '''Leopoldt's conjecture''' states that the <math>\mathbb{Z}_p</math>-module rank of the closure of <math>E_1</math> embedded diagonally in ''U''<sub>1</sub> is also ''r''<sub>1</sub> + ''r''<sub>2</sub> – 1.

Leopoldt's conjecture is known in the special case where ''K'' is an [[abelian extension]] of <math>\mathbb{Q}</math> or an abelian extension of an imaginary [[quadratic field|quadratic number field]]: [[James Ax|Ax]] reduced the abelian case to a ''p''-adic version of [[Baker's theorem]],{{sfnp|Ax|1965}} which was  proved shortly afterwards by Brumer.{{sfnp|Brumer|1967}} [[Preda Mihăilescu|Mihăilescu]] has announced a proof of Leopoldt's conjecture for all CM-extensions of <math>\mathbb{Q}</math>.{{sfnp|Mihăilescu|2009}}{{sfnp|Mihăilescu|2011}}

[[Pierre Colmez|Colmez]] expressed the residue of the ''p''-adic [[Dedekind zeta function]] of a [[totally real field]] at ''s''&nbsp;=&nbsp;1 in terms of the ''p''-adic regulator.{{sfnp|Colmez|1988}} As a consequence, Leopoldt's conjecture for those fields is equivalent to their ''p''-adic Dedekind zeta functions having a simple pole at ''s''&nbsp;=&nbsp;1.
